title: Isn’t the sea what Algy calls it: a grey sweet mother?
html_source:
“Algy” refers irreverently to Algernon Charles Swinburne, English pre-Raphaelite poet, whose poem “The Triumph of Time” contains the lines:

I will go back to the great sweet mother,
Mother and lover of men, the sea.

Buck is slightly misquoting, probably on purpose: he quotes the line accurately later in the passage.

Actual serious painting of Swinburne by William Bell Scott

‘Grey’ was a typesetter’s error for ‘great’.
